memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah. His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver sprinkling bowl weighing seventy shekels, both filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering; one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs a year old to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab. - Num 7:12-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the first day, Nahshon of the tribe of Judah brought his offering. Judah went first — the same tribe that led the march and camped toward the sunrise. And his offering was generous and complete: silver, gold, grain, and animals for burnt, sin, and fellowship offerings. It was a full and costly gift.

Someone has to go first. Going first takes courage; there is no example ahead to follow, no one else to hide behind. Nahshon stepped forward and set the pattern of glad, wholehearted giving that all the others would follow. His willingness to lead made it easier for the rest.

We can be grateful for the people in our lives who "go first" — who give first, serve first, step out in faith first, and show the rest of us the way. And perhaps God is calling you to be that person in some situation: the first to give, the first to forgive, the first to volunteer, the first to obey.

There is something deeper here too. From this tribe of Judah, the Lord Jesus would come — the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:5). And Jesus is the great "first" of our faith. He gave first, loved first, and offered the complete and final sacrifice. "We love because he first loved us" (1 John 4:19).

Whatever God may be asking of you, remember that Christ has gone first. Follow His example, and do not be afraid to lead the way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is God calling you to "go first" in some area?
- Who has led the way for you by their example?
- How does Jesus, who "first loved us," give you courage?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You went first, loving and giving before I ever did. Give me courage to lead the way in generosity, faith, and obedience. Amen.
